scope: Selected verbatim accessibility-text excerpts from actual browser responses, not complete transcripts; UI text may truncate long paragraphs. Reviews are static and did not execute hardware or repository tests.
input_summary: Five-case brief with current local measurements: sequential draft/verify; same-prompt request ratios 0.892/0.934 and identical k trajectories; native and FP32 replay widths and exactness; historical token-29 2x2 cache/current-width test; isolated projection reproduction; shared-host low-power conditions. Asked for conclusions, confounds, falsifiers and bounded unusual experiments. Correction messages clarified ratio definitions, unchanged full-request timing boundaries, unproven causal attribution, and absence of unobserved-width counterfactual data.

initial_invalid_excerpts: Furthermore, computing time ratios against a scalar serial baseline calibrated on a different prompt invalidates the sub-unity (0.892 and 0.934) speedup claims.

C4 Zero-Pad Dispatch Proof: I withdraw claiming that a zero-padded input test can prove the internal Metal kernel dispatch branch; establishing dispatch selection requires MLX source inspection and kernel instrumentation.
gemini.transcription_note: Spacing normalized in excerpts. The second item above is a withdrawal in the correction response, retained alongside the invalid claim it addresses.
corrected_excerpts: C1 Producer Pipelining Limit: I withdraw implying that a single-block producer halting until verifier commit overlaps draft generation during target verification of that block.
C3 Ratio Direction & Derived Thresholds: I withdraw treating C3 ratios as per-step latency multipliers, along with all derived break-even acceptance thresholds and the 1.66 cross-lane threshold.

It does not prove this single element delta alone caused the position-29 argmax flip (11136 vs 279), nor that linear projections are the sole source of batch-width divergence across attention and KV state.

Same-Prompt A/A Noise Floor & In-Request Controller Calibration (C2/C5): Measure paired target-only A/A full-request ratios across the prompt suite to quantify host variance, and replace external-prompt scalar calibration with online measurement of the current prompt's prefill/decode step cost before admitting draft execution.
coordinator_rejections_after_correction: The correction still converts 1-ratio into elapsed-time slowdown percentages. That conversion is incorrect; paired elapsed-time increases must be computed from the raw pairs.
Both original and charged full-request timers already include startup, rewind and cleanup. Their timing difference cannot be attributed to a changed request accounting boundary.
A matched prompt pilot does not prove which overhead caused the net slowdown, and a primitive intervention still needs downstream and cache-history controls.

initial_excerpts: No code was executed and no sources are claimed; every number below comes from your five cases only.
Both preserve exact target verification and full cost accounting; both leave paradigm decisions deferred until the matrix is complete.
coordinator_rejections: The initial response confuses full-replay time ratios with per-step ratios and calls the policy timing difference accounting sensitivity despite identical full-request timing boundaries.
FP32 diagnostic equality does not isolate the mechanism to floating parameters alone: dtype changes affect arithmetic and kernel paths.
One isolated projection delta does not establish that this delta caused the final target argmax flip. High-precision tolerance checks do not diagnose a kernel defect or prove pinning will work.
One observed k trajectory does not reveal counterfactual acceptance and costs for every unobserved width.
corrected_excerpts: Static review; no hardware executed. Corrections accepted.
Unobserved widths have no measured costs or acceptances; one logged trajectory cannot price them. Every k comparison requires executed runs.
FP32 exactness on three prompts does not localize the cause to floating parameters: a dtype change alters arithmetic and kernel paths across the graph.

The isolated layer-0 projection establishes a reproducible shape-dependent numerical delta at that primitive, not that this delta caused the final argmax flip; multiple later projections and attention can differ.
coordinator_rejections_after_correction: The old and charged paths are not strict A/A replicates: instrumentation differs even when k trajectories match. Aggregate ratios 0.892 and 0.934 are not two raw A/A samples and cannot estimate a noise distribution.

Fixing one intervention and restoring one argmax would be scoped to that prefix and intervention; it would not prove a unique original cause, global batch invariance or preserved serial-reference semantics.
